An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 8.2
div.ab: Quin etiam de bosco, de prato et aquis et molendinis, parcis, uiuariis, piscariis, uirgultis et hortis et negotiationibus et omnibus rebus, quas dederit Dominus, decima pars Ei reddenda est, qui nouem partes simul cum decima largitur.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 632 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: Moreover, from wood, from meadow and waters and mills, parks, fishponds, fisheries, copses and gardens and trade and all things which the Lord has given, the tenth part is to be rendered to Him who bestows the nine parts together with the tenth.
